**Issue #4508 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4508: Patch: the fuzz monitor fails a game in which a Spell changes a Unit Immune to Spells, and a test casts every Spell at one
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Some Units are Immune to Spells: no Spell may target them or change them in any way. The game keeps breaking that promise in small ways. Until this week, a Spell that buffed every Unit or picked a random card still changed the protected Unit. Each case was found by someone reading the code, one card at a time. One case is still live: the four War Doctrine Spells ("for the rest of the game, your Units have Trample" and the like) still give their keyword to a protected Unit.

Once this is built, the random games that run on every change watch for it. When a Spell changes a protected Unit, the run fails and names the Spell. A new test also casts every Spell in the game, on both faces, at a board with a protected Unit on each side. A card that breaks the rule then fails on its own pull request instead of reaching players.

## Why

- §6.1's row (`spec/06-keywords.md:47`) says Immune to Spells means "Spells can't target it or affect it". Every Spell's effect list skips it, "every Unit, every field card of a card scope and a random pick of the field included" (R4453000).
- The engine enforces the rule walk by walk: each walk of the field must remember to ask `restrictions::unaffected_by` (`crates/engine/src/restrictions.rs:67`). R4453000 records that "several other walks of the field never asked". #4476 fixed about a dozen Spells (Core #28, Core #48, C #70, C+ #40, C+ #50, M #34, S #3, S+ #32 and S+ #103 among them), and every one was found by reading. Two more fixes for the same keyword are open now (#4424, #4484).
- One case is still live on `main`. `lent_by_player` (`crates/engine/src/layers.rs:195-213`) lends a `UnitsHaveKeyword` player modifier's keyword to every Unit its controller has. The modifier records no source (`PlayerModifier`, `crates/engine/src/state.rs:809`), so S #137.1 to #137.4, the War Doctrines (Spells), give Trample and the others to a Unit Immune to Spells. R1859007, the Doctrines' ruling, never mentions immunity.
- Dormant cards had the same history and got a check: I19 (#4454, #4487; `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs:81-89`, `slumber_reach_findings` at `:1159`) fails any step in which an event reaches a Dormant card. Nothing watches Immune to Spells: none of the monitor's twenty checks reads the keyword, and no test in `crates/cards/tests/cross/` does either.
- Random games rarely bring the two together. 17 card scripts name the keyword (Paragon-X prints it, and Cloaking Module's Radiant face adds it), against 371 Spells (289 cards and 82 tokens) in `crates/cards/catalog.json`. That is why a fixed, repeatable sweep comes with the check.

## Proposal

1. **I21 in the monitor**, built the way I19 is, reusing its `reached_ids` (`invariants.rs:1074`) and its tracking of the card running (`hookResolving`, `trapFired`, turn edges).
   - `before` notes each field Unit that is Immune to Spells, by its layered keywords, as the step begins.
   - `after` walks the step's events. While the card running is a Spell (its face's printed type in the catalog, not a Field Spell), an event that names a noted Unit is a finding: `I21 Spell reached Immune to Spells: <event> names <card> on turn N in <spell>'s run (§6.1, R4453000)`.
   - A Unit is judged only if it is still on the field and still immune after the step, so an aura dropping mid-step makes no false finding.
   - The check reads the event stream and the catalog, never `unaffected_by` (the file header's rule: "an oracle, not the fix restated").
2. **Lawful windows, each with a ruling** in the issue's block, decided the way R4454000 and R4454002 decided I19's:
   - a board swap, a rotation or a board restore that carries the immune Unit;
   - a Spell's forced attack, whose target is struck by the attacking Unit (Units still reach it);
   - anything else the first runs turn up.
   A window is narrowed to fix a false finding, never dropped.
3. **Run it everywhere I19 runs**: every 1v1 wave on the played path, I14's branches against the state each was reduced from, and each Duos duel's monitor.
4. **The sweep**, in `crates/cards/tests/cross/invariants.rs` beside I19's module at `:3341`. For every Spell and Spell token in the catalog, base and Radiant:
   - the board: the Spell in seat 1's hand at full mana, with `stand-in (1) 4/4 Immune to Spells` and a plain stand-in on each side;
   - the plays: each play of it that `legal_actions` lists, capped as I14 caps them, its prompts answered by a seeded policy;
   - each step runs through the monitor, and no I21 finding may show;
   - the board holds only stand-ins with no text, so the sweep also holds each immune stand-in's whole `unit_view` (keywords, attack, health, position, controller) to what it was, for every step whose only runs were Spells'. That catches a change no event names, such as the Doctrines' lend.
5. **Fix what it finds in the same pull request.**
   - The Doctrines first: the modifier records that a Spell made it, and `lent_by_player` passes an immune Unit by, with a ruling that settles R1859007's reading.
   - Then every Spell the sweep or the fuzz fails, each fix with its test and, where the spec does not already decide it, its ruling.
   - If the list runs long, split the work as `docs/issues-and-patches.md` (A task over every card) says.
   - The pull request carries a table with one row per Spell that did anything other than pass the immune stand-in by: the card, fixed or lawful, and why.

## Where it lands

- `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` (I21 and the header's list) and `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs` (hand-built cases)
- `crates/cards/tests/cross/invariants.rs` (the sweep)
- `crates/engine/src/layers.rs`, `crates/engine/src/state.rs` (`ModifierKind::UnitsHaveKeyword`) and `crates/engine/src/effects/player_mods.rs` (`give_units_keyword`, `give_units_keyword_next_turn`), plus any other walk or card script the check finds
- SPEC §6.1 (the Immune to Spells row), `spec/rulings/R<issue>…`, `spec/pending/<issue>.md`, and the list of checks in `crates/engine/README.md` and `crates/tools/README.md`
- A pending patch fragment (`cargo jackioh patches`) for each card that plays differently

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] I21 is in the monitor and in its header's list. Hand-built tests show it fail on a Spell that buffs an immune Unit on the field.
- [ ] Hand-built tests show I21 pass on each of these: a Unit's Cry that buffs it; a Field Spell's or a Trap's effect on it; a Spell that buffs a copy of it in a hand; a Spell whose step first takes its immunity away.
- [ ] Each lawful window has a ruling note whose `proven_in` lists a test named after it.
- [ ] The sweep plays every Spell and Spell token on both faces, with its count asserted against the catalog so a new Spell joins on its own. It finds no I21 and no changed `unit_view` on an immune stand-in.
- [ ] A Doctrine cast beside an immune Unit leaves that Unit without the keyword, while a later Unit of the caster still gets it, in a test named after its ruling.
- [ ] The fuzz gate passes with I21 on at CI's 200 seeds, in its handicapped wave and in its Duos wave. The pull request states the gate's time before and after, and the sweep's own time.
- [ ] The pull request's table lists every Spell the check turned up, with its verdict.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.

## Size and risks

Hard (CLAUDE.md rule 11: engine rules, and a fix whose card count is unknown until the sweep runs). I19's pull request (#4487) added about 1,500 lines across the monitor and its tests.

- **False findings:** a hook with no marker of its own inside a Spell's run would be blamed on the Spell. The fix is a tighter window or a new marker, never a dropped check.
- **What it cannot see:**
  - A Spell's delayed effect carries no `hookResolving` (see the header of `hook_marks.rs`), so I21 cannot reach it.
  - A Spell that only reads an immune Unit changes nothing on it, so neither check sees it. Example: C #43 Plague Nuke counts the Plague Counters on every Unit, including an immune one it did not destroy (`c043_plague_nuke.rs:28-43`). That case is left for a ruling of its own.
- **Replays:** every fix changes play, so an old replay in which it mattered is refused as `rules_changed` (R767000), as R4453000's were.
- **Overlap:** #4459 and #4500 touch the same keyword, so build on `main` once they land.

## Steps

1. Re-read the touched ground: `spec/06-keywords.md:47`, `spec/rulings/R4453000.md`, `R1859007.md`, `R4454000.md`, and the I19 block (`testkit/invariants.rs:995–1305`, `2315–2365`, `2942–3070`, `3660–3795`, `4519–4545`).
2. Record the lend's source. In `state.rs`, add `from_spell: bool` to `ModifierKind::UnitsHaveKeyword` with a serde default so stored states still read, and cite R4508001. In `player_mods.rs`, set it from `restrictions::effect_is_from_spell(ctx)` inside both `give_units_keyword` verbs (this covers every caller, including the training-grounds one, with no per-card flag). Update the `view_for.rs:1317` match arm. Rejected: a hardcoded `true`, which would misjudge any future non-Spell caller.
3. Skip the protected in the lend. In `layers.rs`, add `immune_without_lend`: true when `card_keywords` plus `conditional_keywords_of` plus `aura_mods` keywords hold Immune to Spells. It must not call `unit_has`/`unit_view`, which would recurse through `lent_by_player`. `lent_by_player` returns nothing for a Unit where the modifier's `from_spell` is true and `immune_without_lend` holds; all other lends are unchanged.
4. Build I21 the way I19 is built, reusing `reached_ids`. `immune_step(state)` notes every field Unit with layered Immune to Spells (`unit_has`), by id with label and side, plus the pending resume. `runs_a_spell(after, def_id)` is true when either printed face's type is Spell (both faces of a Spell card are, Field Spells never are) or a fused ingredient runs one, mirroring `is_board_sweep`/`copies_a_sweep`. Walk each step's events tracking `running` across `hookResolving`, `trapFired`, turn edges and the pending resume exactly as I19 does. An event naming a noted Unit while `running` is a Spell is a finding — `I21 Spell reached Immune to Spells: <event> names <card> on turn N in <spell>'s run (§6.1, R4453000, R4508000)` — except the lawful windows, each citing R4508000: `attackDeclared` never counts (an attack is Units reaching, §4.2); damage-family events with `combat: true` never count (strike-back included); `controlChanged`/`bounced` (and Restore's `radiantSet`) inside a `swapped`/`rotated`/`rolledBack` window never count, mirroring I19's `BoardMove`; `radiantSet` under `radiant_world` never counts. Judge only Units still on the field and still immune after the step, so immunity lost mid-step makes no finding. Wire `note_immune` into `before`, take the step in `after`, chain `immune_reach_findings` in `listed_refused` beside I19's, and note the other duel's state in Duos `before`. Update the header's "twenty checks" to twenty-one with an I21 paragraph in I19's style.
5. Prove the monitor by hand in `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs`, using the `freeze.rs` fixtures (a Spell freezing every enemy Unit, a 2/4 warded Unit) and the `spell_verbs.rs` pattern: `r4508000_…` failing on a Spell buff/freeze of an immune field Unit; passing on a Unit's Cry buff, a Field Spell's effect, a Trap's effect, a Spell buffing a hand copy, a step that first removes immunity, a forced-attack combat, and a board-swap carry. Name every test after its ruling and list each file in that ruling's `proven_in`.
6. Rule it. Write `spec/rulings/R4508000.md` (I21 and the windows above) and `R4508001.md` (a Spell's "your Units have" lend passes immune Units by; the later-arriving Units still gain it; amends R1859007's reading), each with `proven_in` naming the tests. Put the §11 paragraphs in `spec/pending/4508.md`, link R4508001 from the §6.1 row, update both README check lists, run `cargo jackioh spec check`.
7. Sweep every Spell in `crates/cards/tests/cross/invariants.rs`, copying the census idiom of `activate_listed.rs:296–340` (`CATALOG.iter`, `set_ships`, both faces). For each Spell id and each of base/radiant: a fresh `scenario` with the Spell in seat 1's hand at the stock full-mana value (grep `"mana":` in `cross/` and copy it), `stand-in (1) 4/4 Immune to Spells R4/4 Immune to Spells` and a plain `stand-in (1) 4/4 R4/4` on each side. Drive each listed play (`plays_of`, at most `I14_ACTION_CAP`, in listed order), answering prompts with the first option bounded exactly like the Comet Crash idiom at `invariants.rs:1476–1499`, stopping a play whose reduce errors. Run each step through the monitor (`before` with the played body, `after` on its events) and fail on any I21. Hold each immune stand-in's whole `layers::unit_view` across every step whose markers are all Spell runs (or none) and fail on any change — this catches the silent lend no event names. Assert the swept set equals the catalog's shipping Spell set so a new Spell joins on its own.
8. Fix what the sweep and fuzz smoke find: Doctrines first, via steps 2–3, with `r4508001_war_doctrine_lends_no_keyword_to_an_immune_unit_but_lends_to_a_later_one` in `c137_1_land_doctrine.rs` (cast beside an immune Unit: no keyword on it, keyword on a Unit arriving later; no I21). Each further fix gets its test plus `R4508002…` where the spec does not already decide it. Keep the PR table: one row per Spell that did anything but pass the immune stand-in by — fixed or lawful, and why. Reads-only Spells (C #43 Plague Nuke counting counters on an immune Unit) stay unchanged for a ruling of their own, as the issue orders.
9. Claim the play changes: `cargo jackioh patches "<title>" --source <issue-or-PR> --notes <what-changed> --plays <ids>` for the Doctrines and each fixed card, hand-writing each `player` note. Record the fuzz smoke time before and after on the same seeds plus the sweep's own time for the pull request.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' r4508000` — the I21 fail case plus every pass case and window in step 5.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-cards c137_1 r4508001` — Doctrine lends nothing to the immune Unit, lends to a later arrival.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-cards --test cross i21` — the sweep and the Spell census.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' i19` and `cargo test -p jackioh-cards --test cross i19` — I19 untouched.
- `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine -p jackioh-cards --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo jackioh catalog check`; `cargo jackioh patches check`; `cargo jackioh spec check`.
- Smoke only: `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 5`, `--handicap --seeds 2`, `--duos --seeds 2`. CI runs the 200-seed, handicapped and Duos gates.

## Done when

- [ ] I21 is in the monitor and its header list; the hand-built fail test fails without the monitor change and passes with it.
- [ ] All five pass cases hold (Cry, Field Spell, Trap, hand copy, immunity removed mid-step), each lawful window has a ruling with a same-named test.
- [ ] The sweep plays every shipping Spell and Spell token on both faces, count asserted against the catalog; zero I21, zero changed immune `unit_view`.
- [ ] The Doctrine test holds: no keyword on the immune Unit, keyword on a later arrival.
- [ ] `spec check`, `patches check`, `catalog check`, fmt and clippy green; fuzz smokes pass; the pull request states gate times before/after, the sweep's time, and the per-Spell verdict table.

## Risks

- A hook with no marker of its own inside a Spell's run is blamed on the Spell (same over-attribution I19 accepts); tighten the window or add a marker, never drop the check.
- Delayed effects carry no `hookResolving` and Spell reads change nothing, so I21 sees neither; both stay out of scope by design.
- `immune_without_lend` deliberately excludes the lend layer to avoid recursing through `unit_view`; any future immunity source outside printed, granted, conditional and aura keywords must join it.
- Every behavior fix changes play, so affected old replays refuse as `rules_changed` (R767000), as R4453000's did.
- Overlap: #4424, #4484, #4459 and #4500 touch the same keyword — build on `main` once they land and re-run the sweep.
- Per-step layered keyword reads cost gate time; the pull request must show the gate within its budget.

## Open questions

None. Every choice the task leaves open is decided above; anything the first runs turn up (a new window, a new failing Spell) gets a narrower window or a fix with its own `R4508002…` ruling, never a dropped check.
```
